Axiom:
Session key = (spec, phase kind). Within ONE spec, hold ONE long-lived worker session per phase kind actually present in its tickets (`impl` / `test` / `config` / `bootstrap` / `doc` / `refactor`) — the next phase of the SAME kind in the SAME spec redispatches into that SAME session instead of a cold start. Different kinds ALWAYS get different sessions: a session that wrote code MUST NOT see the context of the session that wrote tests, or vice versa — no peeking.
Every dispatch message MUST stay self-contained regardless of continuation: resend the exact same 3-line activation a first-time dispatch would get (directive path · ticket + phase · "run `sdd-task --phase` and follow its output") — reusing a session is a context optimization, never a substitute for the instruction; every task arrives as if from a cold start. This is what makes context overflow and compaction harmless: state lives in files (ticket, Execution Log, Handoff, `sdd-task --phase` output), never in conversational memory.
Batch parallelism has two independent gates: the tickets' Target Files are disjoint AND their next worker session keys `(spec, kind)` are different. The same key owns one mutable long-lived session, so dispatches sharing it serialize even when their Target Files are disjoint. Different keys never override a Target-File overlap.
Reuse is an optimization with a mandatory environment-agnostic fallback: not every environment can continue a subagent session. Where continuation is available, redispatch by key; where it is not, raise a fresh worker with the SAME message. Correctness never depends on which path ran — the missing capability is not a blocker and never a reason to change the flow.
Reset to a fresh session even where continuation is available: (a) a fix dispatched from an audit / code-review finding — fresh eyes only, the session that wrote the bug is the wrong one to re-look at it; (b) a spec or group switch — sessions close together with their group, one spec's context MUST NOT leak into the next spec's session. Also reset whenever the orchestrator loses the key→session mapping (restart, compaction) — raising a fresh session there is safe by the same file-backed state guarantee, never a correctness risk.
